_about: Prince built from his parts (tasks/02). Metres; +x his right, +y forward, +z up. Each part is a soft volume; all are blended into one surface by tools/parts.py.

parts.name: body
parts.note: the big round body: from the front a wide round mass, widest a little below the middle; from the side an egg longer than tall, highest behind the head, rounding down into the haunches; from behind nearly a circle (master, sheet 01, 03, 05, 07, 09, close-up 08). Proportion pass: set further back and higher at the rear (sheet 03: his back is high and round right to the rump; sheet 09: his body runs further back), and a little narrower (master)

parts.name: head
parts.note: the round head on the front of the body, no neck: from the front narrower than the body at eye level and merging into it below; from the side its face comes forward of the chest and its top is about as high as his back (master, close-ups 06, 25, 08, 10; sheet 01, 03, 07, 09). Lower and narrower at eye level than first tried: in the master his head is narrow between the ears and at the eyes (the eyes sit on its sides), and its top is well below where the first try put it; the width below the eyes is his cheeks (step 3). Tipped nose-down ~12 deg: in the profiles (sheet 03, close-ups 08, 10) his face slopes down from the eye to a nose below eye level

parts.name: crown
parts.note: broad, flattish top of the head: in the master the top of his head between the ears is a wide, nearly flat arc about as wide as the eyes are apart, not a narrow dome (master, close-ups 06, 25, 14). Kept above eye level so it does not bury the eyes

parts.name: ear
parts.note: short rounded ear, set wide apart on the top-back of the head, tips leaning out and a little back; about 2 cm above the head (master, close-ups 13, 14, 06, 25; sheet 03, 05, 14). Blocked in as a soft flap now; shaped (cupped, thin) in step 8 (mirrored). Set further back, fuller and leaning back more: in the right profile his ear sits well behind the eye and is taller than it looks from the front (it leans back, so the master foreshortens it)

parts.name: temple
parts.note: the wide back of the head behind each eye: from the front his head is widest at and just below eye level, with fur beyond the eyes, so the eyes sit inside his outline; from above his head is broad behind the eyes, not a narrow snout (master, close-ups 06, 25, 14; sheet 09) (mirrored)

parts.name: muzzle
parts.note: the broad, blunt lower face: from the front a wide soft muzzle under the nose, no narrow snout ridge (master, close-ups 06, 25, 27); from above the face ends blunt and round (sheet 09, close-up 11); from the side the nose is only a little ahead of the cheek (sheet 03, close-up 21). Proportion pass: smaller and set forward-low, so from the side the face tapers forward and down to a small nose (close-ups 21, 02; sheet 03) instead of ending in a blunt wall; the breadth from the front is the cheeks behind it

parts.name: jowl
parts.note: whisker pads and chin under the nose, filling between the cheeks: from the front his face below the nose is full and soft with no hollow (master, close-ups 06, 25, 27); from the side the lower face curves back under the nose into the chest (close-ups 21, 02)

parts.name: bib
parts.note: the full chest bib under the chin: from the side the front of his body under the face is one full round curve with the face resting on it, no notch under the muzzle (sheet 03, 07, close-ups 08, 10, 16); from the front a broad soft bulge below the mouth (master, sheet 01, 11, 12). Set back: in the profiles his chest is well behind the nose, the jaw sloping back and down to it

parts.name: skirt
parts.note: the lower skirt: from the front his body is a rounded square, sides nearly straight and the base broad and flat on the floor, with the peets just peeking out (master, sheet 01, edited front set); from behind and the side the base is broad too (sheet 03, 05). Higher, rounder and softer than first tried: his base rolls under softly; the first try made a hard ledge

parts.name: cheek
parts.note: full round cheeks: from the front his face is broad right under the eyes and flows straight out into the body (master, close-ups 06, 25); from above the head is blunt and nearly as wide as the body at the cheeks (sheet 09); from the side the cheek fills under the eye down to the chest with no undercut (sheet 03, close-ups 08, 10, 21) (mirrored). Set lower (below the eyes, not over them): the first try buried the eyes. Broader and a little higher (but flatter, so it stays under the eyes): from the front his face is nearly as wide as his body from the eyes down, a rounded square, not a pear; blended a little wider so the sides run smoother (too wide buried the eyes), and set a touch lower. Set back a little, so the face in profile is a wedge to the nose, not a vertical wall

parts.name: floor
parts.note: he sits on the floor: a soft flat underside

eyes.note: provisional, from the eye fit (true size from the profiles); seated properly in step 9
